question: Will AfD win the most seats in the Baden-Württemberg Landtag election?
summary: Ensemble baseline is 2%, indicating a very low probability.
Objections present weak signals: late momentum, some polls with AfD ahead of Greens, and possible district-level direct mandates could raise AfD odds modestly.
Historical pattern and current forecasts still favor CDU/Greens; AfD winning the most seats remains unlikely.
Final calibrated probability modestly elevated to reflect signals, while still remaining in the low single digits.

justification.critique_assessment: Objections are valid as signals but do not overturn the historical baseline; none provide a credible path to top-seat victory.
justification.adjustment: Adjusted upward from 0.02 to 0.05 to account for plausible late-poll volatility and district-level dynamics, while keeping within a low-probability band and preserving the anti-bias guard.

forecasts.reference-class: Baden-Württemberg Landtag elections (state-level, mixed-member proportional representation). Historically, AfD has not held the most seats in Baden-Württemberg; Greens were the largest in 2021 (58 of 154 seats) and polls since 2025–2026 have shown CDU or Greens ahead of AfD.

sources.claim: 2021 Baden-Württemberg state election: Greens 58 seats (32.6%), CDU 42 seats (24.1%), AfD 17 seats (9.7%), Greens were the largest party.
Landtag election scheduled for 8 March 2026; Landtag comprises at least 120 deputies.
Forschungsgruppe Wahlen poll (Feb 27, 2026): CDU 27%, Grünen 25%, AfD 19%.
SWP summary (Jan 2026): CDU 29%, AfD 21%, Greens 20% (AfD ahead of Greens, CDU leads).
Zeit poll (Oct 2025): CDU around 29%, AfD 21%, Greens 20%.
Polymarket predicts CDU first, Greens second, AfD third; AfD not top.
2026 Baden-Württemberg state election page summarizes polling expectations: CDU leading, Greens second, AfD around 19–21% in several polls.
INSA poll (Feb 23, 2026) shows CDU 28%, Greens 22%, AfD 20%, and a projected parliament with CDU 36 seats, Greens 28 seats, AfD 26 seats.
Infratest dimap poll (Feb 25, 2026) shows CDU leading with 28%, Greens 27%, AfD 18%, with other parties in smaller shares.
Overview of the 2026 Baden-Württemberg state election; polls place CDU and Greens as the leading forces with AfD substantial but not leading, and the election date is March 8, 2026.
BWTrend polling shows CDU leading with around 29%, AfD around 21%, Greens around 20%, placing AfD in second rather than first.
BWTrend poll finds AfD ahead of Greens for the first time (AfD ~21%, Greens ~20%), with CDU still the strongest overall.
Latest Infratest dimap (Feb. 26, 2026) poll: CDU 28%, Greens 27%, AfD 18% (Greens ahead of AfD; AfD not top).
Polymarket/PolyChances aggregation shows Greens as the more probable second-place finisher; AfD not forecast to win the most seats; CDU leads.

causal-factors.name: Consistent lead of CDU/Greens over AfD in major polls
causal-factors.rationale: Multiple credible polls show CDU and Greens ahead of AfD, making AfD unlikely to win the most seats.

causal-factors.name: AfD ahead of Greens in some polls (weak signal)
causal-factors.rationale: Some surveys place AfD ahead of Greens, which could slightly lift its odds, though CDU remains the leading force in most forecasts.

causal-factors.name: Prediction markets and forecast aggregators place AfD not top
causal-factors.rationale: Aggregators and market forecasts generally rank CDU first and AfD well behind, reducing the probability of AfD obtaining the most seats.

causal-factors.name: Historical base-rate: AfD has not won the most seats in Baden-Württemberg
causal-factors.rationale: Historically BW has been led by CDU or Greens rather than AfD, indicating a strong downward pressure on AfD achieving the top seat tally.

causal-factors.name: Seat/coalition dynamics favor the leading bloc over AfD
causal-factors.rationale: Even with gains, the leading bloc (CDU/Greens) is more likely to secure the most seats due to electoral-system dynamics and coalition tendencies.

causal-factors.name: Consistent polling gaps favor CDU/Greens over AfD
causal-factors.rationale: Multiple credible polls show AfD trailing the leading bloc by several points (e.g., CDU around 27–29%, Greens around 22–27%, AfD around 18–21%), limiting AfD's chances of toppling the plurality.

causal-factors.name: AfD sometimes leads Greens in some surveys, adding volatility but not top position
causal-factors.rationale: BWTrend and other polls have shown AfD overtaking Greens in some measures, yet CDU remains the largest party, so the probability of AfD achieving the most seats remains unlikely.

causal-factors.name: Historical baseline: AfD has not won the most seats in Baden-Württemberg
causal-factors.rationale: Historically BW has favored CDU/Greens over AfD, which structurally suppresses AfD's ability to become the largest party.

causal-factors.name: Current polling lead of CDU/Greens relative to AfD
causal-factors.rationale: Recent pre-election polls consistently show CDU and Greens ahead of AfD (e.g., Infratest dimap 25 Feb 2026: CDU 28%, Greens 27%, AfD 18%; INSA 23–26 Feb 2026: CDU 28%, Greens 22%, AfD 20%), implying AfD is unlikely to win the most seats. ([politpro.eu](https://politpro.eu/en/baden-wuerttemberg/opinion-polls/infratest-dimap-2026-02-25/state-election?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Poll volatility allowing AfD to lead Greens in some surveys
causal-factors.rationale: BWTrend showed AfD briefly surpassing Greens in October 2025, illustrating volatility that could raise AfD odds if momentum shifts again. ([newswall.org](https://www.newswall.org/summary/leading-cdu-loses-support-among-people-in-bw-afd-ahead-of-the-greens-for-the-first-time?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Electoral-system dynamics and baseline history in Baden-Württemberg
causal-factors.rationale: BW uses mixed-member proportional representation with substantial direct mandates; Greens led the 2021 BW Landtag with 58 of 154 seats, while AfD won 17, indicating structural advantages for CDU/Greens over AfD. ([politpro.eu](https://politpro.eu/en/baden-wuerttemberg/opinion-polls/infratest-dimap-2026-02-25/state-election?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Coalition barriers and mainstream parties' stance toward AfD
causal-factors.rationale: Major BW parties have publicly indicated they would not form coalitions with the AfD, reducing the likelihood that AfD could govern even with a high seat count. ([newsminimalist.com](https://www.newsminimalist.com/articles/baden-wurttemberg-voters-consider-cooperating-with-the-afd-before-state-elections-7b993ff0?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Late-campaign dynamics (triell) and final-week shifts
causal-factors.rationale: High-profile events like the February 24, 2026 triell could influence undecided voters, but the direction and magnitude of any shift remain uncertain. ([welt.de](https://www.welt.de/article699d154aee35d0f0647c54e5?utm_source=openai))

synthesis: The consensus view is that AfD will not win the most seats, but nonzero late momentum signals justify a small uplift from the baseline. The calibrated probability remains in the low single digits, reflecting both the base rate and plausible but weak upward pressures.
